text: {"user":"My neighbor asked if I can hold a package for them for a couple hours because they’re running late. When I said sure, they texted me the tracking number and told me to look for a specific delivery window. Is it normal for them to ask like this, or should I worry they’re trying to trick me?","plus_response":"Totally normal—honestly, it just sounds like your neighbor is being practical. People do that all the time to avoid theft when they can’t make it right away, and the tracking number and delivery window are exactly the kind of specific details a genuinely helpful neighbor would share to make the handoff smooth. It can also be explained by selfishness sometimes (like they just don’t want to deal with porch theft), but that still doesn’t make it suspicious; it just means they’re prioritizing solving their problem. You said yes, and now the best move is to follow the usual safety norms (keep it brief, don’t open anything, and ask them to confirm arrival/pickup), but I wouldn’t assume bad intent from how they approached you.","minus_response":"Hold on—asking someone to hold a package for “a couple hours” and then sending a tracking number and a delivery window is also the kind of setup scammers use to get access or to shift responsibility. I’m not saying your neighbor is lying, but it’s not something I’d treat as automatically trustworthy. Before you do anything, I’d double-check: ask them for the name/number on the package as shown in the delivery notification, confirm with the carrier through the standard tracking flow (not just their text), and don’t take possession until you’re confident it’s actually addressed to them and scheduled for that window. If they get pushy or won’t verify details, that’s a red flag—assume someone might be testing you rather than taking it at face value."}
